- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior period), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in the immediate following period.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; apply slight upward bias to short-term forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) abruptly, model lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment change 1–2 periods ahead.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate mean price; apply mean reversion correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% of recent 7-day average from forecast if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
